edges.label: CIA history confirms the 1952 flap drove Agency intervention
edges.note: Haines records the escalation from the summer 1952 sightings through Chadwell's memoranda to the January 1953 panel.

a.label: A Die-hard Issue: CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-1990

edges.label: CIA states the Air Force made misleading and deceptive public statements
edges.note: Haines writes that reconnaissance-programme secrecy 'led the Air Force to make misleading and deceptive statements to the public' — an agency of the US government confirming official deception on this subject.

edges.label: Black aircraft generated real cover stories
edges.note: CIA's own historian states that U-2 and OXCART flights accounted for over half of late-1950s and 1960s reports and that false explanations were issued to protect them.

b.label: A Die-hard Issue: CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-1990

edges.label: CIA published its own institutional history of its UFO role in 1997
edges.note: Gerald K. Haines, the Agency's historian, published an eighteen-page account in Studies in Intelligence acknowledging the OSI effort, the Robertson Panel and the later U-2/OXCART attribution.

edges.label: CIA convened and sponsored the panel, and concealed that sponsorship
edges.note: The panel was convened by the Office of Scientific Intelligence. The CIA's own history states that any mention of Agency sponsorship of the panel was forbidden.

edges.label: CIA convened and staffed the January 1953 scientific advisory panel
edges.note: Convened by the Office of Scientific Intelligence under H. P. Robertson; the panel recommended debunking and the monitoring of civilian UFO groups.

edges.label: Assistant Director for Scientific Intelligence who drove the CIA's 1952-53 UFO effort
edges.note: Chadwell's OSI memoranda are the internal record of CIA's decision to treat the subject as a security and public-opinion problem.

edges.label: Chadwell assembled the panel with Robertson
edges.note: The CIA's own official history states that in January 1953 Chadwell and H. P. Robertson put together the panel of nonmilitary scientists to study the UFO issue.

edges.label: CIA's official history documents the panel's debunking and concealment
edges.note: Haines records the mass media and Disney recommendations and states plainly that CIA sponsorship of the panel was forbidden from being mentioned.

edges.label: Denial is the public face of concealment
edges.note: CIA's own historian records that false explanations were issued knowingly to protect classified overflights; the denial is the output of the concealment activity.
